clip: The surface is clipped at log2 264 = 18.80 bits, the entropy of the uniform model over all 264 = 456,976 strings. This is a display convention, not a physics statement: 18.80 bits is the largest entropy any four-letter distribution can have, so it is a natural reference level, and nothing about the model stops energies from rising above it. Clipping draws every cell at or above 18.80 bits at exactly that height so the deep wells remain visible; a cell at the ceiling is more improbable than a uniform random string, and its true (higher) energy is shown on hover. What clipping hides is precisely the tail you would inspect to see how far above the plane a cell sits — hover reveals the true value, and no data is discarded.
above_max: 18.80 bits is a bound on the entropy S = ⟨E⟩ = ∑w P(w)E(w) — the probability-weighted average energy — not on any individual energy. E(w) = −log2 P(w) grows without bound as P(w) → 0, and a bin's Ebin = −log2(P(bin)/|bin|) exceeds 18.80 bits exactly when the bin's average occupancy P(bin)/|bin| is below the uniform level 1/264, i.e. the bin is emptier than a uniform slice. Since S2 ≈ 7.5–9.4 bits is far below 18.80 bits, most mass sits at low energy, and the identity S = ∑ P E forces the remaining mass onto strings with energies well above the mean — necessarily above 18.80 bits. This is a generic property of any non-uniform distribution, not a finite-sample artefact; the one finite-sample feature is that exact-mode forbidden strings sit at E = +∞.
smoothing: The smoothing is a rendering step only. The binned values Ebin are computed exactly (each is −log2 of a sum of exact model probabilities), and the smoothed surface is a deterministic function of those bins. By the data-processing inequality, a deterministic function of the data cannot carry more information about the model P than the bins themselves, so smoothing adds nothing. Interpolation between measured bins can invent spurious wells or barriers, and extrapolation into unmeasured regions is unconstrained. The surface is Boltzmann-domain kernel regression (a Gaussian kernel applied to 2−E, so deep wells survive the average and barriers are lowered), with the length adapting to local variation. Grey cells are cells onto which no string projects (|bin| = 0): Ebin is undefined there and no model probability sits there — read grey as absence of data, not as high energy.
heatmap: The 2-D “top” view is the same Ebin surface seen from above: colour = Ebin in bits, x/y = the two projection axes. It is the same kind of picture as the free-energy maps in BioEmu (Lewis et al., Science 389, 6761, 2025, doi:10.1126/science.adv9817), which plot protein free energy in the plane of the two slowest time-lagged independent components (tICA) of the sampled structures. Here the coordinates are the two principal axes of the fitted model's letter-indicator covariance: each word is placed by which letters it holds at which positions, words differing by common substitutions land near each other, and basins appear as dark low-energy regions separated by light barriers. The axes differ in kind — ours is a static variance decomposition, BioEmu's a kinetic (time-lagged) one — so the analogy is to the type of map, not to its coordinates.
sb_vs_new: This artifact shows two models, kept strictly separate. S&B model (tabs 1 and 2): Stephens & Bialek's pairwise maximum-entropy (Potts) model of fixed-length four-letter words, fitted by exact enumeration of all 264 strings, with single-letter-substitution moves. New (augmented) model (the remaining tabs): the same maximum-entropy principle lifted to words of varying length on one grand-canonical energy scale, with substitution, transposition, insertion and deletion moves, approximate fitting for long words, and all 41 Twitter shards. Read the S&B tabs and the augmented tabs as two studies of one idea at different resolutions, not as one interchangeable model — do not carry a number from one into the other.
